about.title: Petaluma Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Sonoma County recorded 3 traffic deaths in Petaluma during the most recent full year, alongside 193 injury collisions across corridors like US-101, E Washington Street, and both Mcdowell Boulevards. Behind each of those numbers is a family trying to make sense of a loss that arrived without warning. California law gives certain surviving family members, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, the right to bring a wrongful death claim, with other dependents or heirs eligible in some situations. These cases run on a separate track from any criminal charges the responsible party might face. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we connect grieving families in Petaluma with an independent attorney who can explain standing, deadlines, and what losses may be recoverable. There's no obligation to move forward, and no fee unless the case results in a recovery. Reaching out costs you nothing but a few minutes.

items.title: Standing Is Limited by Law
items.desc: California restricts who may file a wrongful death claim, prioritizing spouses, domestic partners, and children before other dependents or heirs. An attorney can help determine where your family fits.

items.title: The Clock Starts at Two Years
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter window. Missing these deadlines can end a family's ability to recover anything at all.

items.title: Civil and Criminal Cases Run Separately
items.desc: A wrongful death claim is independent of any criminal prosecution tied to the incident, and the outcome of one doesn't determine the other. Families can pursue compensation regardless of criminal proceedings.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may qualify under certain circumstances. An independent attorney can review your family's situation and clarify who has standing.

items.question: How long do we have to file after losing a loved one in Petaluma?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. If a government entity, such as a city or county road authority, may be involved given a collision on a road like N Mcdowell Boulevard, the deadline is considerably shorter. Speaking with an attorney early helps preserve your options.

items.question: What can a wrongful death claim actually recover?
items.answer: Recoverable losses typically include funeral and burial costs, the financial support the deceased would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. No claim can undo the loss, but it can help address the financial strain that follows. An attorney can walk through what applies to your family's circumstances.
